newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati fails to answer police summons.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati fails to answer police summons.

text.p: Megawati Sukarnoputri, the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), did not appear for police questioning on Thursday because of faults in the summons, her lawyers said.
Megawati was to have appeared at the South Jakarta police station to answer questions about a function she held at her house in January to celebrate the party's 24th anniversary.
Witnesses said about 50 Megawati supporters held banners and chanted slogans outside the police station on Thursday morning before peacefully dispersing without incident.
"The summons does not specify who are the suspects in the case or who are the witnesses," Megawti's lawyers said in a letter to the South Jakarta police chief, Lieutenant-Colonel Sisno Adiwinoto.
Megawati's husband, Taufik Kiemas, represented by the same team of lawyers, also failed to answer a police summons on Wednesday with his lawyers citing personal reasons for his non-attendance.
The lawyers said the summonses also lacked the necessary presidential approval because Megawati and her husband are both members of the House of Representatives.

Adiwinoto told reporters on Wednesday that if the pair did not appear at the time specified they would be summoned again. Under Indonesian law, if they ignore three summons police can detain them for questioning.
The lawyers said Megawati has been summoned as a witness in the matter of the alleged illegal political gathering.
Megawati was ousted as PDI leader at a government-backed congress last June. Surjadi, who the congress chose to replace her, held the party's anniversary meeting in Central Sulawesi.

Police also questioned Megawati last year as a witness in connection with the riots on July 27 in Jakarta, which were sparked by a police raid on the party's headquarters after it was attacked by Surjadi's supporters. No charges were filed.
At least five people died in the riots, the worst in Jakarta in two decades.
